bull.b: An 81.5% revenue jump combined with industry-leading gross (~89%) and net (~31%) margins signals a durable transition from development-stage losses to a scalable, high-margin commercial model. This structural profitability supports sustained R&D funding, commercial reinvestment and improved returns over multiple years.

Extremely low leverage and a large equity/asset base provide strategic flexibility to fund late-stage trials, launches and potential M&A without immediate financing. Coupled with a multi-billion dollar cash balance, the strong balance sheet materially lowers solvency and refinancing risks for the next several years.

VYVGART’s seronegative approval, high prefilled‑syringe adoption and >5,000 repeat neurologist prescribers reflect entrenched commercial traction. These structural advantages expand the addressable base, accelerate earlier-line adoption and increase lifetime patient value, supporting durable top-line growth across indications.

bear.b: Although cash flow quality improved in 2025, prior multi-year negative operating and free cash flow shows the business historically relied on external capital in down cycles. Persistent earnings-to-cash conversion variability raises risk that future investment needs or trial delays could pressure liquidity without steady cash generation.

Sustained near‑term operating spend nearing $1.0B reflects necessary investment to expand indications and commercial footprint, but creates structural margin vulnerability. If clinical readouts or launch uptake slow, the fixed-cost base could compress profits and limit optionality for future program prioritization.

Heterogeneous diseases (myositis, CIDP) and exploratory or subset-driven results increase the probability of ambiguous or delayed pivotal outcomes. This structural development risk can slow label expansion, raise program costs and complicate payer adoption, making long-term peak-sales outcomes more uncertain.
